_doc: Medium batch m01 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10). Spiders, scorpions, centipedes/millipede and beetles. New motifs live in motifs/medium_m01.js; every piece (unique and class) has a hand note.

orb-spider.notes: Garden orb spider: a round tan spider sitting at the hub of a dewy wheel web; it waits, drops on a dragline and wraps its catch.

p.u0: Web Snare: small wheel webs hang at spots, tied together by silk lines, the spider waiting at each hub

u1.n: Venom Fang: the spider drops off the edge on its dragline, wheel and all, to bite

p.u2: Silk Wrap: white silk-wrapped bundles hang along the edge and twirl on their threads

u3.n: Orb Spin: a row of wheels spins up along the edge, dew running down the spokes

p.b0: Silk Wheel Snare: wheel webs are flung off the edge and spin out

b1.n: Patient Lunge: the spider rushes down its radial line in one run, the dragline behind

b2.n: Orb Web Screen: dewy orb webs held up in a row as a screen, beads flicked off

b3.n: Line Drop Lure: the spider bobs on its line at spot after spot, luring

fishing-spider.notes: Fishing spider standing on the water film: long banded legs splayed, a dimple ring under every foot; it darts, dives and snatches minnows.

p.u0: Water Skim: banded legs splay and the spider skates out and back, dimples under each foot

u1.n: Dive Snare: spiders hold spots under the film, tied by a silk line, bubbles rising

u2.n: Silk Float: the spiders sit in a row on silk rafts, water beads running along the line

p.u3: Float Pin: one spider darts the length of the edge over the water and pins, dimple rings behind

b0.n: Minnow Dive Strike: a silver minnow is flicked up out of the water

p.b1: Water-Walk Rush: legs reach off the edge in a rush, dimples popping

b2.n: Bristle Leg Guard: hairy banded legs held out like a fence, water beads flicked off

p.b3: Surface Skim Feint: the spider blinks from dimple to dimple across the surface

golden-orb-weaver.notes: Huge golden orb weaver: long jointed legs and a long gold body walking on strong golden silk that glints in the sun.

u0.n: Gold Silk Wall: two golden strands draw along the edge, the long-legged weaver standing guard on them

p.u1: Web Dodge: the weaver steps out along its gold lines and back again
p.u2: Orb Bite: the weaver drops below its gold strands to bite, falling away

u3.n: Hammock Rest: little golden silk hammocks rise and sway

p.b0: Golden Fang: long golden legs strike out over the strands

b1.n: Silk-Wrap Sting: gold-wrapped bundles are flung off the edge

b2.n: Gilded Silk Sheet: the gold strands are held taut, a white glint crossing

b3.n: Path-Wide Snare: gold lines tie spot to spot across the path

dune-scorpion.notes: Sandy desert scorpion: comes up out of the dunes, tail curled over in a question mark, claws forward; sand everywhere.

p.u0: Tail Sting: curled tails stab down off the edge and fall away, venom bulbs pale

u1.n: Claw Grab: a pair of sandy claws runs the edge snapping shut

p.u2: Plate Up: tails curl over in a row like raised shields and hold

u3.n: Sand Shuffle: the scorpion shuffles under, sand waves heave out and settle

b0.n: Pincer Snip: sandy pincers snap out off the edge

p.b1: Curled Question Sting: question-mark tails rear and strike outward

b2.n: Sand Carapace: tails tuck down along the edge, fine sand sifting off the plates

p.b3: Sideways Scuttle: the tail pops up at a new spot each blink

whip-scorpion.notes: Vinegaroon: slim black body, two big feeler arms, a long thin whip tail; sprays sour vinegar mist and sidles at dusk.

u0.n: Whip Lash: thin whip tails lash out and crack, a yellow spark at the tip

p.u1: Acid Sup: curled whips rise off the edge in a puff of vinegar mist

u2.n: Dusk Hide: slim bodies slip out and back under a dusk haze

p.u3: Tail Lift: the whip lifts high and the body slams down

b0.n: Whip-Arm Snip: the thick feeler arms snip their way along the edge

b1.n: Sour Spray Jab: a vinegar jet squirts from the tail base

p.b2: Flat Vinegar Shell: flat dark bodies line the edge, whips laid back
p.b3: Mincing Sidle: the slim body sidles from spot to spot, whip trailing

giant-centipede.notes: Giant forest centipede: a long orange body rippling in an S, yellow legs, big poison fangs at the head; very fast.

p.u0: Hundred Legs: orange bodies lunge off the edge, yellow legs rippling
p.u1: Venom Jaws: fangs open and the bodies drop away, poison falling
p.u2: Coil Up: bodies curl tight along the edge and hold

u3.n: Hundred Steps: one long body races the length of the edge

b0.n: Hundred-Leg Nip: the head darts out, fangs snap, and pulls back

b1.n: Forked Foot Sting: the body runs the edge, sting marks where the hind feet strike

b2.n: Segmented Plate: armoured segments line up along the edge, a sheen on the plates

p.b3: Many-Legged Rush: bodies flicker from spot to spot in a blur of legs

cave-centipede.notes: Pale eyeless cave centipede: a slower, ghost-white sibling of the giant centipede with huge legs; drops from the roof among dripping stalactites.

p.u0: Cave Strike: a pale eyeless body shoots along the edge on huge legs, damp beads running
p.u1: Moist Rest: cool drips rise and bead off stone tips
p.u2: Stalactite Cover: stone teeth grow out along the edge, drips forming and falling

u3.n: Roof Drop: pale bodies drop off the edge like falling from a cave roof

p.b0: Roof-Drop Nip: the pale head lunges out, fangs open

b1.n: Pale Draught Sting: pale bodies strike through a cold draught haze

p.b2: Cave-Pale Carapace: pale stone teeth line the edge like a carapace
p.b3: Roof-Lurk Slither: the pale body slips in and out of the dark at spots

giant-millipede.notes: Huge black millipede with red legs: glossy coils that unroll into a wave of legs and curl back up; slow and heavy, poison mist when startled.

p.u0: Ring Crush: black coils slam out, red legs rippling, and drop back
p.u1: Coil Armour: tight glossy coils sit along the edge and hold

u2.n: Poison Mist: yellow-green defensive mist curls up off the edge

p.u3: Startled Curl: coils snap shut and red legs bristle out
p.b0: Curl-Up Nip: a coil unrolls and nips out off the edge

b1.n: Red-Leg Sting: coils lunge out, red legs jabbing

b2.n: Coiled Black Shell: glossy coils hold the edge, sheen flecks

b3.n: Startled Coil Roll: a curled millipede rolls along the edge

scarab-roller.notes: Sacred scarab: a gold-green beetle pushing a huge ball like the sun, head down and stubborn.

u0.n: Gold Carapace: scarabs pop out from behind their balls and back, a gold glint crossing

u1.n: Sun Roll: a rayed sun ball rolls the length of the edge, the beetle pushing

p.u2: Sacred Ball: sun balls held in a row, rays turning slowly
p.u3: Scarab Ball Shove: big balls are shoved out and thump back, dust flying
p.b0: Sun-Ball Pinch: scarabs lunge out from behind their balls

b1.n: Beetle Horn Jab: the beetle rams its ball out and back like a horn jab

b2.n: Gold-Green Armour: balls and shells hold the edge, sheen flecks

p.b3: Stubborn Ball Roll: balls pop up at spots and keep rolling

bombardier-beetle.notes: Bombardier beetle: orange head, shiny blue-black shell, a tail turret that swings round and fires boiling steam with a pop.

p.u0: Hot Spray: beetles aim down and boiling drops fall in a puff of steam
p.u1: Repair Rest: resting beetles rise, steam wisps curling off

u2.n: Armour Plate: shiny blue-black shells line the edge, sheen flecks

p.u3: Turn Cannon: tail turrets swing out like spikes and pop steam
p.b0: Boiling Tail Puff: steam puffs pop off the edge

b1.n: Scalding Jet: a beetle runs the edge, a hot jet squirting

b2.n: Shiny Carapace Sheen: shells held along the edge, a white glint crossing

p.b3: Aimed Shot Lineup: beetles blink into spots and aim their turrets

ember-beetle.notes: Ember beetles: a swarm of small beetles glowing like live coals, sparks lifting, a scorched track behind.

p.u0: Ember Spit: glowing coal beetles spit, embers falling and fading
p.u1: Hot Shell: coal backs flare out like spikes of heat
p.u2: Cinder Rush: a swarm of live coals scurries off the edge

u3.n: Scorched Track: a coal beetle runs the edge, scorched footprints behind

b0.n: Coal-Glow Nip: glowing beetles dart out and back

b1.n: Hot Coal Sting: a hot beetle runs the edge, sting flashes

p.b2: Glowing Shell Plate: coal backs line the edge, glowing
p.b3: Ember Scurry: coals blink from spot to spot

frost-beetle.notes: Frost beetles: blue-white glinting domes that skate on ice, rime needles on their backs, frost creeping where they pass.

u0.n: Rime Charge: frosted shells charge off the edge, snow flying

u1.n: Ice Skate: one shell skates the whole edge, a white skid line behind

p.u2: Frost Plate: frost shells line the edge, rime needles growing
p.u3: Bowling Ball: shells tuck and bowl out, thudding back
p.b0: Frost-Shell Nip: shells lunge out, glints sliding

b1.n: Ice-Edge Sting: shells strike out, a hard white glint

b2.n: Frozen Shell Guard: frozen shells hold the edge, a glint crossing

p.b3: Ice-Skid Bowl: shells skid from spot to spot

lava-beetle.notes: Lava beetles: heavy black plates split by glowing red cracks, magma oozing, heat shimmer; stubborn and unstoppable.

p.u0: Magma Plate: black plates push out like spikes, red cracks glowing between
p.u1: Cinder Shove: cracked plates slam out and drop back, magma beads oozing

u2.n: Ash Cloud: grey ash puffs bloom out and hang, blinding

p.u3: Stubborn Track: cracked plates hold the edge, heat shimmer above
p.b0: Scorch-Track Nip: plates lunge off the edge, cracks flaring

b1.n: Cracked-Glow Sting: a glowing plate grinds the length of the edge

b2.n: Red-Cracked Carapace: plates hold the edge, embers rising from the cracks

b3.n: Unstoppable Scorch Run: a plate scorches along the edge, embers behind
